subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I notice the koala isn't actually gripping the branch properly—its arms float out sideways rather than wrapping around the fork, and the body position creates an odd intersection with the trunk crotch rather than a natural hugging pose.

The arms themselves look like broken shards because of how the box-section sweeps twist at the joints. I'll switch to simple rod geometry with square cross-sections (sides:4) between shoulder-elbow and elbow-wrist, with small cubes at the joints to hide gaps and keep the blocky pixel-art aesthetic.

Checking the geometry, the wrist position lines up with the branch fork so the hand box overlaps the limb correctly, which is good. The pose itself needs rethinking though—better to have the koala hugging with arms reaching forward-outward and wrapping around the branch, rather than the current angular wing-like stance.

Legs follow a similar fork-and-joint logic, with hip, knee, and ankle positions tracking the branch geometry, though the feet boxes overlap the limb front enough that they're mostly hidden anyway so I'll leave them. For the head, I'm noticing the eyes are quite small and set high relative to the nose, which is fine for a koala's proportions but worth checking for pixel clarity.

Checking other views: side view leaf cards lean slightly but okay, back view fork limbs form a decent V shape, hips look dark but fine with the cream rump patch. I think the trunk could stand to be a bit thicker since the koala looks like it's sitting somewhat thin and floating—bumping from 0.14 to 0.17 should help ground it better.

Now I'm planning the arm/leg fix: swap the sweep lines for actual rod geometry using the joint positions from the arm chain, connecting shoulder to elbow with tapered radii and square cross-sections for a sturdier look.

Legs get similar treatment with hip-knee-ankle rod radii tapering slightly thinner. Checking the arm joint positions makes sense for a koala-hugging pose, reaching forward and outward before curving back toward the trunk — that reads fine, so I'll move on to fixing the eye textures next.

Adjusting eye box size and position so it sits properly on the head without protruding, nudging the brow up slightly and widening it. Since the eye texture is mostly black it blends into the grey face, so I want to add a lighter halo or white rim ring around the pupil to make it pop visually.

Still writing pixel art pattern...

I'll leave the trunk thickness as-is and write out these edits with precise line changes.
